extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR finvar.lib and ainvar.lib libraries (computational algebraists / invariant-theory practitioners using SINGULAR)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (finvar.lib and ainvar.lib) that compute primary/secondary invariants, orbit/relative orbit varieties, images of varieties, and additive-group invariants; describes usage, assumptions, return types, display behavior, theory notes and examples for each routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary char0
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0(REY,M[,v]); REY: a <matrix> representing the Reynolds operator, M: a 1x2 <matrix> representing the Molien series, v: an optional <int>. Assume REY is the first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien and M the one of molien or the second one of reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bases of homogeneous invariants are generated successively and those are chosen as primary invariants that lower the dimension of the ideal generated by the previously found invariants (see Decker, Heydtmann, Schreyer (1998)). If v != 0 information about stages is displayed. Example given showing typical call and output.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp(REY,ringname[,v]); REY: a <matrix> representing the Reynolds operator, ringname: a <string> giving the name of a ring where the Molien series is stored, v: an optional <int>. Assume REY is the first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien and ringname names a ring of characteristic 0 created by molien or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same successive-basis selection as primary_char0; displays progress if v != 0. Example shows creating a new ring, calling molien, then primary_charp and cleaning up the temporary ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary char0 no molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0_no_molien(REY[,v]); REY: a <matrix> representing the Reynolds operator, v: optional <int>. Assume REY is the first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) and an <intvec> listing some degrees where no non-trivial homogeneous invariants are to be found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generates bases of homogeneous invariants successively and chooses primary invariants that lower the ideal dimension; useful when Molien series is not available. Displays progress if v != 0. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp no molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_no_molien(REY[,v]); REY: a <matrix> representing the Reynolds operator, v: optional <int>. Assume REY is the first return value of group_reynolds or reynolds_molien. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) and an <intvec> listing degrees with no non-trivial invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As above but for char p (ring of nonzero characteristic). Displays progress if v != 0. Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp without
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_without(G1,G2,...[,v]); G1,G2,...: <matrices> generating a finite matrix group, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) of the invariant ring. No Reynolds operator or Molien series is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bases of homogeneous invariants are generated successively and chosen as primary invariants to lower the ideal dimension (Decker et al. (1998)). Example shows calling with generators directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary char0 random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0_random(REY,M,r[,v]); REY: Reynolds operator matrix, M: 1x2 Molien series matrix, r: <int> range parameter (-|r|..|r|) for coefficients of random combinations of basis elements, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of canonical basis choices, random linear combinations of basis elements are chosen as primary invariants to lower the ideal dimension. Displays progress if v != 0. Example demonstrates typical output for r=1.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_random(REY,ringname,r[,v]); REY: Reynolds operator matrix, ringname: name of ring storing Molien series (char 0 ring), r: <int> range for random coefficients, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random linear combinations chosen as primaries; requires ring holding Molien series. Displays progress if v != 0. Example shows creating temporary ring and calling function.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary char0 no molien random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_char0_no_molien_random(REY,r[,v]); REY: Reynolds operator matrix, r: <int> range for random coefficients, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) and an <intvec> listing degrees without non-trivial invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generates homogeneous bases successively and picks random linear combinations as primaries; useful if no Molien series. Displays progress if v != 0. Example included.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp no molien random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_no_molien_random(REY,r[,v]); REY: Reynolds operator matrix, r: <int> range for random coefficients, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>) and an <intvec> of degrees with no non-trivial invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Randomly selects primaries without Molien series in non-modular case. Displays progress if v != 0. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: primary charp without random
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primary_charp_without_random(G1,G2,...,r[,v]); G1,G2,...: <matrices> generating a finite matrix group, r: <int> range for random coefficients, v: optional <int>. Return: primary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Reynolds operator or Molien series used; random linear combinations of homogeneous invariants chosen as primaries. Displays progress if v != 0. Example given.

rubrics_metrics.name: power products
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: power_products(dv,d); dv: an <intvec> giving the degrees of homogeneous polynomials, d: the degree of the desired power products. Return: a size(dv)*m <intmat> where each column contains exponents of corresponding polynomials whose product is homogeneous of degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when assembling power products of primary/secondary invariants; examples show returned exponent matrices for various inputs. No extra options; empty output when no products exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondary char0
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondary_char0(P,REY,M[,v][,"old"]); P: 1xn <matrix> of homogeneous primary invariants, REY: gxn Reynolds operator matrix, M: 1x2 Molien series matrix, v: optional <int>, optional string "old" for backward compatibility. Assume characteristic of basering is zero and REY/M are appropriate returns from previous routines. Return: Homogeneous secondary invariants and irreducible secondary invariants (both <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes secondary invariants by finding a monomial basis of basering modulo primaries, mapping via Reynolds operator, and selecting secondaries (using Gröbner techniques per S. King). The Molien series indicates counts per degree. Internal parameters 'pieces', 'MonStep', 'IrrSwitch' can be tuned to balance memory vs speed; defaults usually fine. If "old" passed, output differs but ideal generated by irreducible secondaries is the same. Displays progress when v != 0. Example shows detailed progress messages and outputs S and IS.

rubrics_metrics.name: irred secondary char0
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: irred_secondary_char0(P,REY,M[,v][,"PP"]); P: 1xn <matrix> primaries, REY: Reynolds operator, M: Molien series, v: optional <int>, optional "PP" to compute power products of irreducible secondaries in all degrees. Assume non-modular case (char(base) does not divide group order). Return: irreducible homogeneous secondary invariants (<matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only irreducible secondaries are computed to save time/memory. If "PP" not used, a Gröbner basis of primaries+irreducible secondaries up to degree d-2 is computed to detect irreducibles in degree d without computing power products. Internal parameters 'pieces','MonStep','IrrSwitch' may be tuned. Displays progress if v != 0. Example shows typical outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondary charp
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondary_charp(P,REY,ringname[,v][,"old"]); P: 1xn <matrix> primaries, REY: gxn Reynolds operator, ringname: <string> naming a char-0 ring containing Molien series, v: optional <int>, optional "old". Assume basering characteristic not zero and ringname was created by molien/reynolds_molien/primary_invariants. Return: secondary invariants and irreducible secondary invariants (<matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As in secondary_char0 but for modular char handling via storing Molien in separate char-0 ring. Uses Reynolds operator and Gröbner-based selection; Molien series indicates sizes. Displays progress if v != 0. Example similar to char0 usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondary no molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondary_no_molien(P,REY[,deg_vec,v]); P: 1xn <matrix> primaries, REY: gxn Reynolds operator, deg_vec: optional <intvec> listing degrees with no non-trivial invariants, v: optional <int>. Return: secondary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculates secondaries by finding monomial basis of basering modulo primaries, mapping via Reynolds operator and using images as candidates. Since Reynolds operator present, this is non-modular case and the invariant ring is Cohen–Macaulay; number of secondaries = product of degrees of primaries divided by group order. For speed/functionality, 'secondary_and_irreducibles_no_molien' may be preferred. Displays progress if v != 0. Example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: irred secondary no molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: irred_secondary_no_molien(P,REY[,deg_vec,v]); P: 1xn <matrix> primaries, REY: gxn Reynolds operator, deg_vec: optional <intvec> listing degrees with no irreducible secondaries, v: optional <int>. Return: irreducible secondary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finds irreducible secondaries by finding monomial basis modulo primaries and previously found secondaries, mapping with Reynolds operator, and selecting irreducibles using Gröbner techniques. Displays progress if v != 0. Example shows progress messages and final IS.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondary and irreducibles no molien
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondary_and_irreducibles_no_molien(P,REY[,deg_vec,v]); P: 1xn <matrix> primaries, REY: gxn Reynolds operator, deg_vec: optional <intvec>, v: optional <int>. Return: secondary invariants and irreducible secondary invariants (both <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines secondary_no_molien and irred_secondary_no_molien behavior. Works in non-modular case (Reynolds operator available); invariant ring Cohen–Macaulay so count of secondaries known from primaries. Displays progress if v != 0. Example demonstrates outputs S and IS.

rubrics_metrics.name: secondary not cohen macaulay
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: secondary_not_cohen_macaulay(P,G1,G2,...[,v]); P: 1xn <matrix> primary invariants, G1,G2,...: nxn matrices generating a finite matrix group, v: optional <int>. n = # variables of basering. Return: secondary invariants (type <matrix>).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used when invariant ring is not Cohen–Macaulay; secondary invariants are generated following Kemper (1996) 'Generating Invariant Rings of Finite Groups over Arbitrary Fields'. Example demonstrates computation in characteristic 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: orbit variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: orbit_variety(F,s); F: 1xm <matrix> defining an invariant ring, s: <string> name for a new ring. Return: a Gröbner basis (type <ideal>, named G) for the ideal defining the orbit variety (the syzygy ideal) in the new ring named s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes algebraic relations of invariant ring generators, eliminates original variables, and returns polynomials defining the orbit variety. Example shows creating new ring and printing G and ring meta-information.

rubrics_metrics.name: rel orbit variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rel_orbit_variety(I,F[,s]); I: an <ideal> invariant under group action, F: 1xm <matrix> defining the invariant ring, optional s: <string> for backward compatibility to call older relative-orbit procedure. Return: without s a list L of two rings; L[1] has weighted degree order and contains a Gröbner basis (G) of the relative orbit variety ideal; L[2] has basering variables plus y(1..m) with a block order and contains G and a Gröbner basis Conv for doing reductions to express invariants in y-variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computes Gröbner basis of relations and eliminates original variables via weighted blockorder (good for quasi-homogeneous ideals). When s provided, calls older relative orbit variety variant. Example demonstrates retrieving rings, G and Conv, and notes about orders/weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: relative orbit variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: relative_orbit_variety(I,F,s); I: ideal invariant under group, F: 1xm <matrix> defining invariant ring, s: <string> name for a new ring. The procedure creates a new ring named s containing a Gröbner basis (G) of the ideal defining the relative orbit variety with respect to I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This older procedure is kept for compatibility but rel_orbit_variety (which uses a different elimination order) is recommended as usually faster. Example prints G in the new ring and gives ordering information.

rubrics_metrics.name: image of variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: image_of_variety(I,F); I: an arbitrary <ideal>, F: 1xm <matrix> defining an invariant ring. Return: the <ideal> defining the image under that group of the variety defined by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls rel_orbit_variety(I,F) and replaces newly introduced variables in output by generators of invariant ring to obtain ideal in original variables that defines image. Example: maps ideal xy to xyz for a given F.

rubrics_metrics.name: invariantRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invariantRing(m,p,q,b[,r,pa]); m: matrix, p,q: poly, b,r: int, pa: string. Precondition: p,q variables with m(p)=q and q invariant under m; i.e., action defined by map m. Return: an ideal containing generators of the ring of invariants of additive group (K,+) given by the vector field m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b>0 compute invariants of degree <= b (and at least one of higher degree) or until all found; if b<=0 continue until all generators computed (use only if ring known finitely generated). If r=1 use alternative reduction. If pa provided, computation pauses when new invariants found and displays them. Algorithm works in char 0 or sufficiently large characteristic. Examples include computing full invariant ring, partial invariants up to degree limit, and demonstration of non-finitely generated case.

rubrics_metrics.name: derivate
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: derivate(m,id); m: matrix (nx1), id: poly/vector/ideal. Assume m is nx1 where n = number of variables of basering. Return: poly/vector/ideal (same type as input) which is the result of applying the vector field defined by m componentwise to id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector field is m[1,1]*d/dx(1)+...+m[n,1]*d/dx(n). Examples show applying to polynomial, vector, and ideal; output formats follow input type.

rubrics_metrics.name: actionIsProper
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: actionIsProper(m); m: matrix (nx1) where n = number of variables of the basering. Return: int = 1 if the action defined by m is proper, 0 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: m defines a group action as the exponential of the vector field m[1,1]*d/dx(1)+...+m[n,1]*d/dx(n). Example usage shown in the library documentation.
